positions.management_story: At 11:51 he posted the level as something for other people - entry 69,446, TPs 73-74k, SL 68k - and said explicitly 'I'm not entering this myself but I think it's worth a try', telling followers to halve risk unless he joined. Seventy-three minutes later he joined: 'Long BTC / Entry: 69.3k CMP / TP: 73k / SL: 66.5k', corrected four minutes after that to 69.4k. Then nothing. The log contains no close, no stop announcement and no PnL card for this trade. The next BTC message, more than twenty hours later, is a fresh call for a long at 67.3k with its own targets and stop, and BTC went on to trade under 65k by the following morning - well through the 66.5k stop.
positions.notes: The single genuinely unresolved position in this window. The events never say how it ended, so outcome is 'unknown' - but price traded far below the stated 66.5k stop within about a day, no card matching a ~69.4k entry appears in the ten-card win-streak recap of 12 June, and he never counts it as a win, so a silent stop-out is by far the most likely ending. The 11:51 plan (msg 329) is folded in here rather than recorded as a separate 'not_taken' call, because it is the same idea at the same level that he took himself an hour later; note that the follower version carried a tighter 68k stop and wider 73-74k targets than what he actually ran.

positions.planned_entry_note: 67.3k CMP - he had to clarify twice that it was a market long, blaming a typing mistake
positions.risk_note: Opened with a soft stop only (manual close on a 4h close under 64.4k), swapped for a hard 65.3k 'to improve R and avoid soft SL', then back to a soft 4h-close stop at 64.6k plus an unspecified hard stop 'somewhere around 63-64k' purely to avoid a liquidation wick.
positions.thesis: Another dip-buy on the way down: long from 67.3k with a 66,550 DCA underneath, on the view that 64.6k was 'the last near biggest support of BTC' and had to hold.
positions.market_context: Continued grind lower through 3 June; he was stacking long attempts as price fell.
positions.management_story: He called the long at 67.3k CMP with 69-70k targets and only a soft invalidation - a manual close on a 4h close under 64.4k. Three hours later he restructured it: a 50% DCA at 66,550, the target tightened to a single 69.3k, and the soft stop replaced by a hard 65.3k 'to improve R and avoid soft SL'. He tightened again to 65k that evening, then reversed near midnight and went back to a soft line - a 4h close under 64.6k - advising a hard stop somewhere around 63-64k only to avoid a liquidation wick. At 03:03 on the 4th the candle closed below it: 'BTC closed below the manual SL you guys can exit if you can't risk no more.' He did not exit with them - 'I'LL PERSONALLY HOLD TILL 63K I believe a temporary bounce is coming' - but ninety minutes later he was opening a fresh long at 62.8k, so his own 63k line had gone too.
positions.notes: No exit price anywhere; the stop is taken from his own announcement that the manual SL had been broken, and the exit time is that announcement. A clear case of guidance diverging from his own action - he told members to close and kept holding to 63k himself, which price then took out (he was longing at 62.8k an hour and a half later). Whether the 66,550 DCA filled is never confirmed, so no average entry is recorded. Worth flagging that this stop and the 1 June one both contradict his later claim (msg 550, 18 June) of the 'first SL of the month on BTC'.

signals.name: Candle-close stops and confirmation (almost always the 4h close)
signals.what_it_is: He treats a candle close beyond a specific price - the 4h close in 35 of 37 cases, the 1h close twice - as the real decision point, publishing stops as 'SL: 4h close under X or hard SL @ Y'.
signals.how_he_uses_it: He gives a 'soft SL' (a 4h close beyond the level) plus a wider 'hard SL' underneath it so a wick cannot take him out, and refuses to accept a stop until the candle actually closes. The same rule is used to stay in a losing trade ('mentioned will wait for 4h close hence I didn't take SL') and to decide whether a level is reclaimed. AUDIT CORRECTION: this is his most-cited piece of chart logic in commentary (35 messages), but it is a minority structure in his published signals - only 14 of 139 signal posts (10%) carry a candle-close stop and only 10 carry the soft+hard pair. Nine signals in ten use a plain numeric stop. It matters most when a trade is going against him, as the reason not to accept a stop.

signals.evidence_notes: Msg 902 leads because it is the clean canonical example. Msg 17 is retained only to document the rare 1h variant - it was previously the lead evidence and first_seen anchor for an item named '4h close', which the audit flagged as an evidence-fit error. Msg 27 ('SL: 4h under 0.59 or hard SLs at 0.581'), the first genuine 4h reference, is dropped from the evidence list because the trader's own numbers in that message are internally inconsistent (the KERNEL entry in the same post is 0.064), so it is an unreliable illustration.

signals.name: 200 EMA (mostly 4h, also 15m/daily) as the line in the sand
signals.what_it_is: The 200 EMA is the only indicator he names repeatedly; holding/reclaiming it is bullish, losing it opens the next leg down.
signals.how_he_uses_it: He converts the 200 EMA into a hard price level and builds the whole trade around it ('we shouldn't lose the 200 ema on 4h that is 77.7k'). A reclaim is a long trigger and a reason to expect repeat bounces; sitting on it is a reason to expect a bounce back to entry rather than take a stop. He also cites EMA 20 and EMA 50 as intraday bounce/rejection points.

signals.name: New daily low sweep then bounce ('dead cat bounce on LTF')
signals.what_it_is: He expects the market to print a fresh daily low, sweep the lows, and then bounce; he buys the sweep.
signals.how_he_uses_it: When BTC is dumping he waits for a new daily low rather than buying into weakness, then longs the bounce and takes a fast 0.5-1R. The same idea appears as 'lows are swept you can add around 25% margin'. Two of his best-timed BTC longs (59.2k on 24 Jun, 58.2k on 25 Jun) came from this. NOTE ON WORDING: he uses 'swept' only once in 1,005 messages (msg 382); the other instances are the same idea in his own plain language ('they'll make a new daily low then bounce it'). The frequency of 5 is a count of the concept, not the word.

signals.name: Prior daily high / daily low as the anchor for both stops and targets
signals.what_it_is: He anchors stops - and, in the other direction, targets - to the prior daily extreme on the trader's own exchange rather than to a structural level.
signals.how_he_uses_it: On shorts the daily high is the stop; on longs the daily low is the stop. He explicitly tells followers to read the level off their own venue because of price differences. The same extreme in the other direction is the natural target ('can visit previous daily high'). AUDIT CORRECTION: the item was previously filed as stop placement only, with a target quote (msg 33) as its lead evidence and first_seen anchor; it now covers both uses explicitly.

reconciliation.summary: His published scoreboard and the reconstructed record do not agree, and the gap is not explained by trade management. Reconstructing every position he posted gives 217 catalogued setups, 200 actually taken, 165 with a knowable outcome: 120 wins, 35 losses, 10 breakevens - 77% excluding breakevens, 73% including them. His own monthly summaries claim 85% (May) and 89% (July). The published figures run 8-13 points hot, and understate the loss count in both months he reported. The direction of travel in the record is real and favourable - monthly win rate rises 73% (May), 76% (June), 82% (July), 83% (August) - so this is a competent trader with a genuinely good hit rate whose accounting flatters an already-good number rather than inventing one. Three structural facts do most of the work: the breakeven bucket disappeared from his summaries once he had an audience, ambiguous outcomes are resolved at his discretion, and whole categories of trade are declared 'unofficial' before the fact.

claimed_vs_reconstructed.reconstructed: 217 setups catalogued, 200 taken, 165 resolved: 120 wins, 35 losses, 10 breakevens = 77% excluding breakeven, 73% including. 35 positions have no recoverable outcome.

why_the_gap: The breakeven bucket disappeared. His pre-server journal recap reported three categories - '25 trades, 22 Wins, 3 BE, 0 loss' (msg 2, 2026-05-06). Every server-era summary reports only Trades / Wins / Losses (msgs 315, 848). With 10 breakeven positions in the reconstruction, folding that bucket into wins alone moves the headline by several points, and it is the single cleanest explanation of the gap.

Ambiguous outcomes are resolved at his discretion, sometimes literally by vote: 'Just checking because I don't know if I should count it as a win or loss as it went to huge profits, I'll pick what the majority says' (msg 403).

The loss count is understated in both published months - 9 claimed vs 13 reconstructed in May, 5 claimed vs 7 reconstructed in July. Losses are the denominator-sensitive term; two missing losses in a 45-trade month is worth about 4 points of win rate.

Whole categories of trade are declared unofficial BEFORE the fact and therefore cannot lose: gold and oil ('I won't count gold trades in crypto summary', msg 405), 5m entries ('Just an idea won't count TP or SL, not an official trade', msg 135), coins he posts but is not personally taking (msg 317), and late-month setups ('Not an official setup, had 40+ setups this month gonna chill rn', msg 843).

Not every trade reaches the server. He concedes it directly: 'I post all my trades in this server but since I wanna grow my X too some of my personal or once in a while trades will be there' (msg 877). Any reconstruction from Discord alone is therefore a subset, and the missing subset is self-selected.

Position-count limits and post-target coasting filter the sample upstream of the tally. He declines setups he rates highly because too many are open (msgs 24, 48, 187, 706), closes trades purely for clutter (msg 769), and stops posting after a good run ('My weekly goal has been done, so I'll take it slow until next week', msg 875). Clutter closures land in the manual-close bucket, which contains no losses.

The reconstruction and his tally are not counting quite the same universe. His May count of 60 exceeds the 54 positions recoverable from the channel; his July count of 45 is one fewer than the 46 recoverable. The two figures drift in opposite directions, which is what you would expect from a hand-kept tally rather than from a systematic bias in the reconstruction.

None of the above requires bad faith, and the reconstruction does not support a fraud reading. It supports a narrower one: the trading is better than average and the bookkeeping is generous, informal, and always generous in the same direction.

how_he_wins.mechanic: Discretionary early exit - he can always choose to book, and he only chooses when green
how_he_wins.explanation: This is the structural fact that produces the win rate. He does not usually leave a resting take-profit; he closes manually when he sees a rejection, a wick, a stall, or simply wants the slot. Because the decision to close is his and the decision to lose is the stop's, discretionary exits are one-directional: they convert unrealised green into a recorded win and never into a recorded loss. Losses can only arrive the one way he cannot veto - through a stop. The cost is that he leaves the tail of every winner on the table, which is exactly why his average R is small.
how_he_wins.numbers: Exit types across 217 positions: manual_close 62, take_profit 45, stop_loss 35, breakeven 11, unknown 43. Of the 62 manual closes, 61 are wins, 1 is breakeven, 0 are losses. All 35 losses closed at a stop. Only 45 of 120 wins (38%) reached a target he had published; at least 26 wins were manual closes booked short of the stated TP. There are more manual closes than take-profits.

how_he_wins.mechanic: A reserved DCA tranche as a rescue tool
how_he_wins.explanation: AUDIT-DOWNGRADED. The draft called the reserved tranche 'the mechanism that turns a losing entry into a winner'. It does rescue individual trades, visibly and sometimes dramatically, but it is used on a minority of positions and the positions that use it perform WORSE than those that do not. It cannot be the engine of the win rate. The reason is not mysterious: a DCA fills precisely when the original entry was wrong, so the cohort is pre-selected for bad entries.
how_he_wins.numbers: 53 of 139 signal posts (38%) publish a DCA level; 57 of 200 taken positions plan one; only 30 (14%) ever fill one. DCA-filled positions: 19W / 9L = 68%. Positions with no DCA fill: 101W / 26L / 10BE = 80% excluding breakevens.

education_and_rules.topic: how to use a position-size calculator
education_and_rules.lesson: Five-step walkthrough: wallet, risk %, entry and SL -> position size, then enter that size manually on the exchange. Demonstrated with the SUI trade at 1% risk, entry 1, SL 0.95.
education_and_rules.quote: How to use it? Step1: Write your wallet Step2: Write your risk % Step3: Write your Entry SL Step4: It gives you a position size, how much coins or margin to long Step5: Go to your exchange manually write down the coins or margin

education_and_rules.lesson: Set the order 'by amount' on the exchange; he demonstrates on Blofin but says every exchange has the same setting.
education_and_rules.quote: Go to your exchanges and set by amount I'm doing this on blofin but every exchange has it the same.

education_and_rules.lesson: If position size is fixed by the calculator, the leverage used is irrelevant to risk - even 500x is fine as long as the same amount is written down.
education_and_rules.quote: A bit if educational posts, simplest way to risk management it can't get any easier. If you use this way you don't have to worry how much leverage to use, you can use even 500x as long as you're writing down the same amount!
